verdicts.why: A machine or organ that stops working is described plainly; no attitude toward it.
Falling short of what was expected is the meaning itself, and 'fail' is the plain default word for it, not a loaded alternative.
'Her courage failed her' states insufficiency without judging the person or the courage.
Not passing an exam is a bad referent named in the plain word; nothing beyond the fact.
'His health is failing' is neutral description of decline.
A teacher failing a student is a plain administrative act; the word takes no side.
A business failing is bankruptcy stated plainly; unpleasant referent, neutral word.
'In the same masterly fashion' is manner or way; the judgement sits in the adjective, not in 'fashion'.
As a vocative it is familiar and can land as patronizing toward a stranger or superior, but I cannot settle whether that is judgement or merely informal register.
The fellow of a glove is one of a pair; pure description.
A botanical part of a corolla; technical and neutral.
The margin of a shell aperture; technical and neutral.
Against 'persuade' or 'induce', 'tempt' frames the inducement as a lure to desire and the act as a yielding rather than a decision, faintly suggesting it is unwise or indulgent.
Names the act of annoying someone in a plain, if formal, word; unpleasant referent, no added attitude.
'The youth of the parish' is young people collectively; neutral.
Freshness and vitality are pleasant by meaning, but the word adds no approval beyond that meaning.
An early period of development, as of an industry; neutral.
'The authorities' names those in control without approving or resenting them.
A transport or housing authority is an administrative unit; neutral.
Speaking 'with authority' names confidence; a positive referent in a plain word.
An authoritative work cited as 'my authority' is a reference, not a judgement.
A private instructor in singing or acting; occupational and neutral.
A passenger railcar; a thing named plainly.
'An embarrassment of riches' means an excess so great it is awkward; the awkwardness is the idiom's meaning, and it does not disparage the riches.
A prominent article in a periodical; neutral journalism term.
A promoted item of merchandise; neutral retail term.
A distinctive linguistic property; technical and neutral.
'Giving her the preference' is the chance to choose or be chosen first; neutral.
To set up or found something is plain description of an act.
To lay the groundwork for something is neutral; no attitude toward what is set up.
